findings.summary: --allow-expiring-rows is gated on a now snapshot taken before the type-back prompt, so a run straddling UTC midnight writes a currently-valid licence into the past ungated.
The headline safety bound (~28 h earlier) is wrong: the PDT fixture moves 31 h and the documented UTC-12 floor moves ~36 h. Repeated twice in REPAIR-RUNBOOK.md.
The revenue-trend sibling regression cannot fail on the pre-fix body under TZ=UTC, which is the environment both CI and the API image run in.
The only proof that EditRunModal is wired to the B59 seam is matched by no command in verifyCommands.
Rows written by UTC+12..+14 devices recover one day early with no code guard, unlike the EXPIRING NOW class.
resolveTenantTimezone is a dead export whose doc comment names a caller that does not exist and hands back the America/New_York fallback the build plan lists as risk #1.
The header states the bug's direction backwards (New York is WEST of UTC), and the opposite direction has no test.
The Date column renders two different date formats in adjacent rows after the B91 swap.
Modified as a sibling of the same defect class with no work package, radius entry or manifest entry.
dateRange's default fromDate is still built from host-local calendar components: the January-1 drop.

The dateRange fix flipped an EXISTING pin: analytics.service.spec.ts:1046 asserted new Date(new Date().getFullYear(), 0, 1) - the defect itself - so that assertion was re-pinned to the UTC anchor with the reason in a comment.

The revenue-trend regression uses a Date stub rather than a process.env.TZ pin: jest hands the sandbox a copy of process.env, so an in-file TZ pin never reaches Node's timezone cache and is inert (measured in this worktree).
